titles.title: Protecting the Rights Of Towns against federal Enforcement contrary to Constitutional Tenets for Immigration Act of 2025

To discontinue a Federal program that authorizes State and local law enforcement officers to investigate, apprehend, and detain aliens in accordance with a written agreement with the Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and to clarify that immigration enforcement is solely a function of the Federal Government.

R. 6890</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20251218">December 18, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="Q000023">Mr. Quigley</sponsor> (for himself, <cosponsor name-id="J000298">Ms. Jayapal</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="M001238">Ms. McBride</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="F000477">Mrs. Foushee</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="N000147">Ms. Norton</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="J000305">Ms. Jacobs</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="O000173">Ms. Omar</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="R000617">Mrs. Ramirez</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="D000096">Mr. Davis of Illinois</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="G000587">Ms. Garcia of Texas</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="G000598">Mr. Garcia of California</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="J000288">Mr. Johnson of Georgia</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="K000385">Ms. Kelly of Illinois</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="W000822">Mrs. Watson Coleman</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="T000481">Ms. Tlaib</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="G000599">Mr. Goldman of New York</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HJU00">Committee on the Judiciary</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To discontinue a Federal program that authorizes State and local law enforcement officers to investigate, apprehend, and detain aliens in accordance with a written agreement with the Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and to clarify that immigration enforcement is solely a function of the Federal Government.</official-title></form><legis-body id="H40A68DBEFD8A44DCBB14FAE564F4E1C7" style="OLC"> 
<section id="HC27BAA3961584B7B8F500EB2103A989C" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Protecting the Rights Of Towns against federal Enforcement contrary to Constitutional Tenets for Immigration Act of 2025</short-title></quote> or as the <quote><short-title>PROTECT Immigration Act of 2025</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="HCD5139D208444DE08A7293877EA55093"><enum>2.</enum><header>Rescission of State and local immigration enforcement authority</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 287(g) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/8/1357">8 U.S.C. 1357(g)</external-xref>) is amended to read as follows:</text>
<quoted-block display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H225395EF3AD64A018DFBD8E60C2067C7" style="OLC">
<subsection id="H7ED6690D54CE452F8A302B0ACD26B76E"><enum>(g)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Except as provided in paragraph (10) of section 103(a), in section 274(c), and in section 439 of the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/8/1252c">8 U.S.C. 1252c</external-xref>), the authority to inquire about or verify immigration or citizenship status and to investigate, apprehend, arrest, or detain an individual for a violation of this Act or any regulation authorized by this Act is restricted to immigration officers and authorized employees of the Department of Homeland Security and subject to limits set forth in other provisions of law.</text></subsection><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> </legis-body></bill>
